prompt: Thiols (R-SH, pKa ~10) are MORE acidic than alcohols (R-OH, pKa ~16). Why?

options.label: S is larger than O, so the negative charge on RS⁻ is spread over a bigger atom and better stabilized
S is more electronegative than O, so S holds a negative charge better
Thiolate (RS⁻) is resonance-stabilized by d-orbital involvement, which alkoxides lack
The S-H bond is weaker than O-H (bond-strength effect), making SH more acidic

explanation: Going down a group: atoms get larger → the conjugate base's negative charge is distributed over a larger volume → more stable (less concentrated charge). Same reason HI > HBr > HCl > HF in acidity. S is actually LESS electronegative than O (2.5 vs 3.4), so option b is wrong. Bond strength does matter but size dominates.
